titel: Hotel near Limburgs Museum | Hotel Asteria Venray
omschrijving: The Limburgs Museum in Venlo is a 24-minute drive from Hotel Asteria in Venray. What you will see there and how to end the day with wellness and dinner.
hero-sub: 250,000 years of Limburg history, opposite Venlo station and a 24-minute drive from your hotel room.
hero-alt: The Limburgs Museum in Venlo with its glass facade by the park
v1-p1: The Limburgs Museum in Venlo is a 24-minute drive from Hotel Asteria and tells the story of Limburg. That story starts a long way back. In the permanent exhibition Van neanderthaler tot stedeling (From Neanderthal to city dweller) you see the remains of a campfire some 250,000 years old and mammoth bones bearing the gnaw marks of Neanderthals.
v1-p2: From there you walk through Roman times and the Middle Ages to the Buggenum coin hoard, found in a field in 2023. In the Historoscoop you take a seat for a panoramic projection that carries you in one sweep through the history of the land between the Meuse and the Rhine.
v1-alt: Large scale model of the fortified town of Venlo in the Limburgs Museum
v2-p1: Alongside the permanent galleries there are changing exhibitions. Until 28 February 2027 you can see Geloof (Faith), with 35 masterpieces from the Rijksmuseum, seen through the eyes of six guest curators. From 10 December to 6 January a hundred nativity scenes fill the foyer, free to visit.
v2-p2: Travelling with children? Head to Feest!, a family exhibition about the festivals of Limburg, from carnival to Ramadan, with dressing-up clothes and a silent disco. For coffee with Limburg vlaai (a local fruit tart) or lunch, there is the museum café, overlooking the Julianapark.
v2-alt: Reconstructed castle wall with a horseman in the gallery about war at the Limburgs Museum
v3-p1: The museum stands on the Keulsepoort, directly opposite Venlo station. For centuries this was where the town's fortifications stood, and later a railway shunting yard. On the south side is the oldest surviving petrol station in the Netherlands, an Esso station from 1933, where you can now get an ice cream. From the museum it is a short walk into Venlo town centre, so a stroll through the town easily turns your visit into a full day out.
v3-alt: Brick facade of the Limburgs Museum with the old petrol station beside it
tip: Book your time slot before you set off, even with a Museumkaart, and park at Q-Park Arsenaal: with the museum deal, parking there is cheaper if you reserve online in advance. Arrive at eleven, then you have the whole afternoon and after closing time you are back for the sauna in half an hour.
g1-tekst: Open from 11.00 to 17.00. The museum is closed on Mondays.
g1-alt: Brick and glass facade of the Limburgs Museum in Venlo, with a lawn in front
g2-tekst: €17.50, ages 4 to 17 €8. Free with a Museumkaart, but you still book a time slot online.
g2-alt: Knight, cannon and scale model of a castle in the Limburgs Museum
g3-tekst: No car park of its own. Q-Park Arsenaal is five minutes' walk away and has a museum deal.
g3-alt: Tower and entrance of the Limburgs Museum with bicycles in front
g4-tekst: Only assistance dogs are allowed inside.
g4-alt: Crucifix and display cases in the Van bijgeloof tot ongeloof gallery at the Limburgs Museum
dag-sub: Breakfast at the hotel, the museum in Venlo during the day and back in the late afternoon for the sauna and dinner.
m1-tekst: The breakfast buffet is served from 07.00 to 10.00 on weekdays and from 08.00 to 10.30 at weekends. The museum opens at 11.00 and is a 24-minute drive away, so there is no need to rush.
m1-alt: Basket of fresh bread rolls on the breakfast buffet at Hotel Asteria in Venray
m2-tekst: Start with Van neanderthaler tot stedeling and the Historoscoop, and have lunch in the museum café. Your time slot is only your start time: you stay as long as you like, until the museum closes at 17.00.
m2-alt: Display case of earthenware jugs in the gallery on living and celebrating at the Limburgs Museum
m3-tekst: Back in Venray, warm up in the sauna. The wellness area is open Monday to Thursday from 16.00 to 22.00 and Friday to Sunday from 12.00 to 22.00. Tuesday is swimwear day.
m3-alt: Foot bath with green mosaic tiles under a skylight in the Top Floor wellness area at Hotel Asteria
m4-tekst: End the day at a table in the hotel brasserie. The kitchen is open until 21.30, and afterwards your room is just a lift ride away.
m4-alt: Bartender pulling a beer at the brasserie bar in Hotel Asteria, Venray
kamers-sub: After a day in Venlo, the sauna and dinner, there is no need to drive home. Choose your room; you see the price for your dates straight away when you book.
kaart-regel: The Limburgs Museum is in Venlo, south of Venray. The map also shows three outings you can combine on the way or nearby.
kaart-alt: Map of North Limburg with Hotel Asteria in Venray, the Limburgs Museum in Venlo and three other outings
f1-v: How far is the Limburgs Museum from Hotel Asteria?
f1-a: It is 27 kilometres, about 24 minutes by car. The museum has no car park of its own. You park at Q-Park Arsenaal or P+R Stationsplein, four to five minutes' walk away. Parking at Hotel Asteria is free.
f2-v: How long does a visit to the Limburgs Museum take?
f2-a: That is up to you. Your time slot is only your start time; after that you stay as long as you like. The museum is open until 17.00, so if you start at 11.00 you have a whole day.
f3-v: Is the museum a good plan when it rains or in winter?
f3-a: Yes, everything is indoors. The museum is open all year from Tuesday to Sunday, 11.00 to 17.00. Different hours apply around the holidays: on 24 and 31 December it closes at 16.00, and on 25 December and 1 January it is closed.
f4-v: Do I need to buy tickets in advance, even with a Museumkaart?
f4-a: Yes. You book a time slot online, even if you get in free with a Museumkaart, the Dutch museum pass; bring the card to the desk. A ticket costs €17.50, ages 4 to 17 pay €8 and children up to 3 go free. These are the prices from November 2026; check limburgsmuseum.nl for current prices.
f5-v: Can I bring my dog, and is the museum accessible?
f5-a: Pets are not allowed inside, assistance dogs are. The museum has lifts, accessible toilets and a ramp to the entrance, and you can borrow a wheelchair there. A companion goes in free.
f6-v: Can I still use the wellness area and have dinner at the hotel after the museum?
f6-a: Yes. The museum closes at 17.00 and you are back in Venray in half an hour. The wellness area is open Monday to Thursday from 16.00 to 22.00 and Friday to Sunday from 12.00 to 22.00. Tuesday is swimwear day. Dinner in the brasserie is served until 21.30.

arcen.desc: Arcen lies on the Meuse, between Venray and Venlo. Around a 17th-century castle, the Kasteeltuinen Arcen (Arcen Castle Gardens) have more than fifteen gardens, including a rose garden, an Oriental water garden and the tropical glasshouse Casa Verde. The gardens are closed in winter; from spring they combine well with a day in Venlo.
arcen.credit: Photos: Vincent van Zeijst and Kasteeltuinen Arcen via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.

hertogjan.desc: Also in Arcen, Hertog Jan brews its beer. On a guided tour you see how the beer is made, from hops and malt to the tasting at the end. Book in advance; the route goes through narrow corridors and up 144 steps.
hertogjan.credit: Photos: B. Hulshoff and Steven Lek via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped; tap photo Hotel Asteria.

maasduinen.desc: Fancy getting outdoors after a day inside? De Maasduinen is a quarter of an hour from the hotel. Between the Meuse and the German border you walk through more than 4,500 hectares of woodland, heath, drift sand and fens. You will find routes at the visitor centre in Well.
maasduinen.credit: Photos: Lieblingsgouda, Steven Lek, Carelbullens and Jonathation via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA), cropped.
